[10] Answer: There are mainly four reasons. Firstly, the scientific challenge(The malaria parasite is very complex. It changes its form seven times during its life cycle and can hide in the human body for days, weeks, months, years, or even decades.) Secondly, the economic challenge (Malaria occurs in some of the poorest and most remote places on Earth. These places may have no roads, infrastructure, electricity, clinics, or clinicians.) Thirdly, the cultural challenge(People in areas with malaria often think of malaria as a normal problem of life. Therefore, they may not take measures such as using bed nets or going to the doctor.) Fourthly, the political problem(It is difficult to get political leaders to do something about malaria.)

Summaries

five sample summaries

[1] Sonia Shah explains why malaria has still not been eradicated even though we have known how to treat and prevent it for a long time. She gives three main reasons. First, malaria is scientifically difficult because the parasite is very complex and can change its form. It can also live inside both mosquitoes and humans. Second, malaria is connected to poverty. People in poor areas are more likely to live in places where mosquitoes can breed, and malaria can also make people poorer because they cannot work when they are sick. Third, malaria has become a normal part of life for many people in affected areas. Because of this, some people do not see it as a serious disease and may not use mosquito nets or visit doctors. Shah also explains that these problems create a political problem. She says that we need to understand people’s daily lives and priorities instead of simply giving them tools from outside. She believes that improving housing, roads, drainage, electricity, and living conditions can help reduce malaria in the long term.
[2] Malaria is an infected disease carried by mosquitoes. Humans have fought with malaria for centuries and we know how to deal with malaria; nevertheless, a number of people around the world have still succumbed to Malaria. The speaker agreed there are three reasons why people overcome this infection even now. First, malaria changes the pattern over many times, so it is difficult for the invention of the medicine to catch up with the changing. Second, it is hard to avoid the place where mosquitoes live.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          
[3] Sonia Shah’s TED talk is about why malaria has not been eradicated even though we have known how to treat and prevent it for a long time. She explains that malaria is a very old and dangerous disease. There are about 300million cases and more than 500,000 deaths every year.Shah explains four main challenges: scientific, economic, cultural, and political/First, the malaria parasite is very complex and can change during its life cycle.Second, malaria is strongly connected to poverty. Poor people are more likely to live in places where mosquitoes can breed, and malaria also makes economic growth slower.Shah says that malaria can reduce economic growth by about 1.3% every year. Third, many people in areas where malaria is common think of it as a normal part of life. Therefore, they may not make malaria a high priority. Shah argues that malaria cannot be solc\\ved only with medicine. Improving housing,roads, drainage, electricity and living conditions is also important.                                                                
[4] She explains three reasons why malaria still exists. It causes about 300 million cases and over half a million deaths per year. First, the parasite is scientifically complex and hard to fight. Second, the disease affects poor areas that lack good roads, electricity, and hospitals. Third, local people think that malaria is a normal disease in part of their life, so they are not interested in malaria and do not use prevention tools such as mosquito nets. In the past, other countries tried to fix this by forcing external tools on them, but it did not work. She says that we cannot beat malaria easily with simple tricks. Instead, just as rich countries did in the past, we must change the way of life by fixing poverty, bad houses, and poor drainage to truly stop the disease.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        
[5] Malaria is a deadly disease caused by mosquito bites, with 300 million cases a year. Journalist Sonia Shah gives three reasons why we cannot get rid of it.First, the scientific challenge: the malaria parasite changes its body 7 times, and mosquitoes live right outside human homes, like in water puddles. Second, the economic challenge: malaria hits poor places that have no roads, no electricity, and no clinics. This depresses economic growth by 1.3% every year. Third, the cultural challenge: people in malarious areas think malaria is a normal problem, just like a cold or flu. So, they do not use bed nets every night.Shah says top-down rules from outside do not work. The best way is to improve housing, roads, and drainage to change the "malarious way of life".                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   
5 Levels: Malaria is a deadly disease caused by mosquito bites, with 300 million cases a year. Opinions

five sample opinions

[1] Watching Sonia Shah's talk reminded me of my own time studying in the Philippines, where I felt how close and real the threat of malaria truly is. Witnessing the situation firsthand made me realize a harsh reality: poverty itself is a major barrier that makes eradicating the disease so difficult. It showed me that solving health crises requires not just advanced medical technology, but also fundamental support to lift vulnerable communities out of poverty and ensure fair access to healthcare.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                
[2] I was surprised to learn that malaria is not only a medical problem but also a social, cultural, and economic problem. I think the most important points in this video is that we should make people’s living environment more hygienic and create solutions that should reflect the needs and lifestyle of local people. Even if mosquito nets are provided for free, they may not be used if they feel inconvenient. This made me think that international cooperation should not simply provide support from the outside. It is more important, we should listen to local communities and understand their situation and culture before taking actions.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       
[3] I was surprised that malaria is connected to many problems besides health. Before watching this TED Talk, I thought that if people had the right medicines and prevention methods, we could make a big improvement, even if we could not completely eradicate malaria. However, I learned that these tools are not always enough. I especially found the cultural challenge interesting. If people experience malaria many times and usually recover, they may think of it as a normal part of life. I think this can also be connected to COVID-19. During the pandemic, we had prevention methods such as masks, but people did not always want to use them. This made me realize that preventing disease is not only about making medicines or tools. We also need to understand people’s daily lives.                                                                                                        
[4] I agree with her opinion. I think why people couldn't be endangered by malaria is not only a medical problem but also something else. Before watching this movie, I think if people have medicine and something to avoid mosquitoes, we could save them from getting malaria. However, poverty, culture and politics are also important. I am especially interested in the idea that some people think malaria is a part of their daily life. This is similar to COVID-19,because people also had to change their daily behavior to prevent infection. I think governments and local communities need to work together, we should also understand the lives and ideas of people in areas where malaria is common. mosquito                                                                                                                                                                                       
[5] After listening to this TED Talk, I was surprised that malaria is still such a serious problem even though we have known how to treat and prevent it for a long time. Before listening, I thought that having medicine and prevention methods would be enough to control a disease. However, Sonia Shah showed me that diseases are also connected to poverty, culture, infrastructure, and politics. I was especially interested in the idea that people may see malaria as a normal part of life. This made me realize that simply giving people a useful tool, such as a bed net, does not always solve the problem. We also need to understand how people actually live and what they think is important. I thought the TED Talk was interesting because it showed that global health problems cannot always be solved by science alone. We need to look at the social conditions behind the problem as well.
